title: Mammootty and Mohanlal Reunited After 18 Years. The Film Flopped. Now It's on ZEE5. Watch It Anyway.
excerpt: Patriot lost ₹60 crore in theatres. But Mahesh Narayanan's surveillance thriller — with Fahadh Faasil, Kunchacko Boban, and Nayanthara — deserves the second chance that streaming gives it.
body:
Let us get the uncomfortable part out of the way first. **Patriot** made ₹80 crore worldwide against a budget of ₹125–140 crore. In Kerala, where it should have been an event, it managed just ₹29 crore in its entire theatrical run. By the end of its second week, the film was adding ₹50 lakh — not per day, but for the entire week. By every commercial metric that matters, Patriot was a disaster.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=LB9lnb3oC2Y</youtube>

Now let us talk about why you should watch it this weekend.

## The Cast That Should Not Have Failed

The last time **Mammootty** and **Mohanlal** shared a screen in a full-length feature film was *Twenty:20* in 2008. Before that, there was *Harikrishnans* in 1998 — the Fazil classic that famously shot two endings because neither fanbase could accept their hero losing the girl. For 18 years, the question in Malayalam cinema has been: will they ever come together again? **Patriot** is the answer, and regardless of what the numbers say, the pairing still crackles.

Mammootty plays **Dr. Daniel James**, a defence scientist who helped build a government surveillance system called Periscope — before discovering it was being used to spy on journalists, activists, and civilians. Mohanlal is **Colonel Rahim Naik**, his old comrade, a retired military officer pulled out of quiet obscurity when Daniel needs someone he can trust with his life. Around them orbits a cast that reads like a Malayalam cinema hall of fame: **Fahadh Faasil**, **Kunchacko Boban**, **Nayanthara**, and **Revathi**.

Director **Mahesh Narayanan** — the man behind *C U Soon* and *Malik* — shoots the whole thing across India, London, and multiple international locations. The cinematography by **Manush Nandan** is gorgeous. The score by **Sushin Shyam** is restrained where you expect bombast. The action, choreographed by a team that includes Dhilip Subbarayan and Stunt Silva, is grounded and tense.

## Why It Did Not Work in Theatres

The reviews were not terrible. *The Indian Express* gave it 3 out of 5. *India Today* went to 3.5. *The Hollywood Reporter India* called it "miles away from greatness but not often do we see a whistleblower thriller with so many unforgettable whistle-worthy moments." The consensus was clear: technically brilliant, thematically brave, narratively uneven.

> "Kudos to Mahesh Narayanan for not being intimidated by Mammootty and Mohanlal's superstardom, and to the two legends for simply trusting the director's vision." — *The Indian Express*

But a three-hour political thriller about spyware and surveillance — however relevant, however timely — is a tough sell at the multiplex. The film opened strong (₹8 crore on day one in Kerala), then dropped 90% in its second week. Audiences wanted the legends together. What they got was a film that asked them to think about digital privacy while sitting in a dark room eating popcorn. The mismatch was structural, not artistic.

## Why Streaming Changes Everything

**Patriot** started streaming on **ZEE5** on **June 5** in Malayalam, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada. And here is where the film has every chance of finding the audience it deserved.

A surveillance thriller works differently on a phone or a laptop. The intimacy of the screen matches the paranoia of the subject. You are watching a film about people being watched — on the very device that watches you. There is something poetic about that, even if Mahesh Narayanan did not plan it.

For the diaspora specifically, this is a significant moment. Most NRIs who wanted to see Mammootty and Mohanlal together did not have access to a Malayalam-language screening in their city. ZEE5 erases that problem entirely. The Hindi dub opens it up further — though, honestly, watch it in Malayalam if you can. The performances are calibrated to that language.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DX034EigW2x/

## The Real Question

The tagline of the film is "Dissent is patriotic." It is the kind of line that sounds like a bumper sticker until you watch three hours of a man losing everything — his career, his safety, his country's trust — because he chose to tell the truth about what his government was doing with the tools he built.

Mammootty, at his best, does not perform moral authority. He inhabits it. There is a quality to his stillness in this film that makes you lean in rather than sit back. Mohanlal, by contrast, brings warmth and physical presence — the colonel who has seen too much and can still throw a punch when it matters. Their chemistry is not fiery. It is the chemistry of two men who have known each other long enough to communicate in silences.

Did the film deserve to make more money? Probably. Is it a masterpiece? No. Is it worth your three hours this weekend, on ZEE5, with a good pair of headphones and no distractions? Absolutely.

Some films need theatres. This one, it turns out, needed your living room.
